builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
summary: LambdaMix replaces training and storing one specialist RL policy per objective weighting (e.g., a set of GRPO checkpoints) with a single run that jointly trains one LoRA adapter per objective over a frozen base, mixed at inference by a preference vector. It costs a group-relative online RL training run (comparable to GRPO, which itself requires reward models, rollout infrastructure, and tuning), plus serving-time logic to combine adapters and weight normalized rewards. It can fail if the preference-conditioned mixture does not interpolate reliably on your objective pair, if the frozen base model limits reachable trade-offs, or if normalized reward weighting produces unstable gradients on objectives with different reward scales.
rationale: The method fits constrained infrastructure (LoRA adapters on a frozen base, fewer completions and stored parameters than multiple specialists), but it depends on online RL infrastructure and task-specific reward design, so its hypervolume advantage must be validated on the reader's own objective pair before production adoption.
technique: Preference-conditioned LoRA adapter mixture for multi-objective RL

claims.statement: LambdaMix replaces training and storing one specialist RL policy per objective weighting (e.g., a set of GRPO checkpoints) with a single run that jointly trains one LoRA adapter per objective over a frozen base, mixed at inference by a preference vector. It costs a group-relative online RL training run (comparable to GRPO, which itself requires reward models, rollout infrastructure, and tuning), plus serving-time logic to combine adapters and weight normalized rewards. It can fail if the preference-conditioned mixture does not interpolate reliably on your objective pair, if the frozen base model limits reachable trade-offs, or if normalized reward weighting produces unstable gradients on objectives with different reward scales.

Achieves higher Pareto hypervolume than conditioned and policy-merging baselines across four models, using fewer training completions and adapter parameters than separate GRPO specialist policies; no multiplicative factor is reported.
